answer: We model Sybil identity multiplication as a cipher over adversarial agents, where each alias must post a dynamic opportunity-cost bond sized to its forgone yield. A subgame-perfect punishment matrix slashes bonds upon deviation, imposing losses that scale faster than any falcon-like fork gain, so the expected payoff of multiplying identities is strictly negative under every gale of entry. Finite bonding and grim-trigger slashing thus converge to a strict Nash equilibrium in which honest participation uniquely survives.
